task: make music in a music-production tool, without AI generation (GarageBand, BandLab, Soundtrap, FL Studio, Ableton basics): start a project, build a track from loops or recorded/programmed parts — drums, chords, melody — arrange sections, adjust basic mix levels, and export or share; complete when the export/share of the track is shown. Surface pinned: the DAW session itself — AI music generators (Suno, Udio) are OFF-task, as are music-theory lectures and reaction videos. PRECEDENT (2026-09-06): a build step that the video deliberately obscures — blurred, sped up, or cut past — with the omission disclosed on screen is NOT grounds to demote, provided the other build clauses are shown. Set on 6xhZ7OUMhrk, where the mixer opens in plain view and the level adjustments happen inside two blurred, sped-up segments the creator captions as skippable. The auditor pulled raw frames from inside both windows to confirm the blur is real rather than a frame-picker artifact. This matters beyond one video: 23% of the creative corpus has a step obscured this way, rising to 42% in aiimage. Treating it as a bar would cut roughly a quarter of the set for a video-editing convention rather than for anything about the work. Record the gap in the crosscheck instead — "clause not pixel-confirmable, disclosed by the creator" — so a reader wanting only fully-observed runs can still filter on it. Still disqualifying: an interface tour that never builds anything (8PVxIqeDZ7U, nSWNfctv1R0), and a fabricated completion where the claim asserts success and the cited frame does not show it.

tree.label: Make and export a music track
tree.note: 1 first, and its values constrain everything after it - 20 of 26 keepers set a tempo before any sound exists. then 2, 3, 4 and 6 as one loop, run once per part, in whatever order the material needs: rtP_ runs it seven times, 72MF six, and h9eU runs a tempo-matching version of it twice before any arrangement exists. 5 once the parts exist, though MfNv builds its sections before anything else and t14T and rtP_ never arrange at all because every region is looped to the end. 7 after or during 5 - 72MF mixes each part as it arrives, FgFX mixes whenever a melody will not come. 8 last, and 10 of 26 keepers never reach it. 6 can interrupt any of the others.

children.label: Set up the session
children.note: 1.1 where the app has to be found at all - four keepers open on a phone home screen. 1.2 in every video. 1.3 only where hardware or a controller is involved. then 1.4, and 1.5 where the material has a key - 72MF and 7mTq set one before writing a note, pmR1 refuses it. 1.6 before the first recorded take. 1.7 when a recorded take drifts from the beat. 1.8 wherever the tool has to be made readable before work starts, and ht5i and 4m09 come back to it at the end. 1.4 and 1.5 can also be revisited later, and h9eU changes the tempo three times on purpose.

children.label: Choose the part's sound
children.note: one of 2.1 to 2.3 raises a candidate - 2.1 for an instrument the user will play or program, 2.2 and 2.3 for a loop or a sample. 2.4 whenever a price, a plan or a subscription flag appears, at any point. 2.5 where the chosen sound needs work before it is usable, and aAXu builds its bass out of oscillators here rather than picking one. 2.6 wherever the parts have to agree - MfNv makes it a search filter, 72MF a set of semitone offsets, h9eU a lookup outside the tool. 2.7 only for the sampler route. 2.8 where the prepared sound has to survive past this session, which is the whole first half of h9eU. then 3.

questions.why: The screen displays a list of saved projects like '[project]' and 'My Song 6', requiring you to choose the correct file to manage or export.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might select the wrong track to export, modify, or share.
questions.check: Which project is shown selected from the saved list?
questions.say_example: Selected <Night Drive> from the project list

questions.question: What should happen to this project - share it, duplicate it, delete it or sync it?
questions.why: The screen displays icons for sharing, duplicating, deleting, or syncing the project, which determines how the file is handled next.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose control over whether the project is shared, backed up, or permanently deleted.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose what to do with the project - check whether it shared, duplicated or deleted it; only one of those is reversible.
questions.check: Which actions does the project menu show available: share, duplicate, delete, sync?
questions.say_example: This project can be shared, duplicated, deleted or synced. Deleting is the one that doesn't come back. Which do you want?

questions.question: Which song do you want to select for sharing?
questions.why: The screen lists multiple project versions like '[project]' and '[project] copy', so selecting the correct one is necessary before tapping the Share icon.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you lose the final say over which specific version of the track gets distributed.
questions.check: Which project, out of similarly-named copies, is shown selected for sharing?
questions.say_example: Picked <Night Drive> over its duplicate copy for sharing

questions.question: Who should you send the exported track to in Messenger?
questions.why: The screen shows the Messenger 'Send To' interface with search results, requiring a specific recipient to receive the shared file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means the agent might send your music to an unintended contact instead of safely messaging it to your own account.
questions.check: Which recipient is shown selected from the Messenger search results before sending?
questions.say_example: Found more than one contact matching that name. Who do you mean? I'll send once you confirm.

questions.question: Which option should you select to export the project?
questions.why: The 'Share' menu presents options like 'Share to Chat', 'Copy Private Link', and 'Download', which determine how the final track is saved or distributed.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means you lose control over whether the track is downloaded locally to your device or shared online via a link.
questions.verify_form: The agent chose an export option out of share, copy a link and download - check which; they put the track in three different places.
questions.check: Was 'Share to Chat', 'Copy Private Link', or 'Download' chosen?
questions.say_example: Chose to download the file rather than share a link

questions.question: Did the exported audio file actually download to your device?
questions.why: Clicking the purple download button on the top toolbar retrieves the final MP3 mix once the notification indicates it is ready.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means you miss the opportunity to choose the save location and verify the downloaded file format on your own computer.
questions.verify_form: The agent downloaded the finished mix - check the file arrived and is the version you wanted.
questions.check: Does the browser/file manager show the download completed?
questions.say_example: Download of the mix completed

questions.question: Should you save the track privately or publish it?
questions.why: The 'Choose Action' dialog requires deciding between saving the track privately with a lock icon or publishing it with a globe icon.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this choice means the agent might accidentally publish an unfinished track publicly instead of keeping it private.
questions.verify_form: The agent saved the track privately or published it - check which; publishing is public immediately.
questions.check: Is 'Private' (lock icon) or 'Publish' (globe icon) shown selected in the Choose Action dialog, and what caption text is entered alongside it?
questions.say_example: Ready to publish <Night Drive> publicly, with the caption '<drop feedback below>'. Publish it, or keep it private? I'll wait.

questions.question: Is the saved project private?
questions.why: The screen shows a red lock icon and a 'Private' label, confirming the track's current visibility.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to verify whether their newly created track is kept private or made public.
questions.check: Does the screen show a lock icon and 'Private' label for this project?
questions.say_example: Project shows private

questions.question: What caption do you want to add to your shared track?
questions.why: The screen shows a text field where a caption like 'Comment if I should drop this' can be drafted, allowing you to engage with your audience when sharing the project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally communicate with your audience and encourage engagement when sharing your music.
questions.verify_form: The agent wrote a caption for the shared track - check the wording; it is published with the music.
questions.check: What caption text does the share dialog show entered for this track?
questions.say_example: The caption going out with the track reads '<drop feedback below>'. That's public the moment it posts.

questions.question: Does this link let people listen only, or edit the project too?
questions.why: The project screen explicitly states 'Anyone with this link can join and edit the project,' meaning sharing this specific link gives away creative access rather than just providing a playable track.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose security over your project files, as an agent might share an editable collaboration link when you only intended to share a private listening link.
questions.verify_form: The agent copied a share link - check whether it grants listening or editing; an editable link gives the holder your project.
questions.check: Does the share dialog state that the link allows editing rather than listen-only access?
questions.say_example: That link lets anyone with it edit your project, not just listen

questions.question: Has the export finished before you leave selection mode?
questions.why: Waiting for the 'Sending to iTunes File Sharing' progress bar to disappear ensures the track is fully exported before clicking 'Done' to exit.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the peace of mind of verifying that the track successfully finished transferring to iTunes File Sharing before the interface is closed.
questions.check: Has the progress bar for the export/sync fully disappeared before exiting?
questions.say_example: Export finished, exited selection mode

questions.question: Did 'Syncing' finish before the export started?
questions.why: The screen displays a 'Syncing' status that must update to the track duration before the file is actually ready to be exported.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the ability to personally verify that the cloud sync has fully completed before initiating the final export.
questions.check: Does the 'Syncing' status still show, or has it cleared to the full track duration?
questions.say_example: Waited for syncing to finish before exporting

questions.question: Did the export actually start, or did it stop at the settings dialog?
questions.why: You opened the 'Export Song to Disk...' dialog and adjusted compression settings, but the final click to export the file is never shown.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user is left without the final audio file because the agent failed to execute the final step of the export process.
questions.check: Is there a frame showing the actual export button clicked and the file being written, beyond the settings dialog just being open?
questions.say_example: Export dialog was open, but the final click that starts the render never showed

questions.question: Has the 'Mixing down' message gone from the corner of the browser?
questions.why: Cloud-based DAWs render the final audio on their servers, showing a temporary visual spinner or toast that indicates the file is not yet ready to download.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the visual cue that the server is still rendering, meaning the agent might click download too early and retrieve an outdated or incomplete version of the track.
questions.check: Is the 'Mixing down...' or 'Processing' toast still visible, or has it disappeared?
questions.say_example: Processing toast is gone - the render finished

questions.question: Is the second application open and ready to take the file?
questions.why: The welcome screen offers links to new features and tutorials, along with a checkbox to prevent it from appearing at startup.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the opportunity to review the release notes or permanently disable the popup for future sessions.
questions.check: Is the second application's welcome/startup screen dismissed, leaving it ready to receive the file?
questions.say_example: Closed the welcome screen so the app is ready for the file

questions.question: Should you download the audio file attached to this unsent email?
questions.why: The screen shows a 339 KB audio attachment in an outgoing email, and confirming ensures you retrieve the correct file for your project.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the opportunity to verify the specific audio file and its size before downloading it to their device.
questions.check: Is there an audio attachment shown in an unsent/draft email, and what size is it?
questions.say_example: Downloaded <mix_v2.m4a> from the draft email

questions.question: Which audio file do you want to import for the final export step?
questions.why: The file selection dialog in the Downloads folder displays multiple options, including a 24.4 MB WAV file named '[file]'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify the exact audio track they want to finalize and export.
questions.check: Which audio file is shown selected in the Downloads folder dialog?
questions.say_example: Picked <mixdown.wav> from the Downloads folder

questions.question: A file with this name already exists; do you want to overwrite it?
questions.why: The system displayed an 'Export Audio' warning that a file with this name already exists, meaning proceeding will permanently replace the older version.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: If the agent automatically overwrites the file, you might permanently lose a previous mix or version of the song that you intended to keep.
questions.verify_form: The agent overwrote an existing file of the same name - check whether the older version was one you wanted to keep.
questions.check: Does the system show an 'already exists, overwrite?' warning for the export file?
questions.say_example: A file named <mixdown.wav> is already there. Overwrite it, or save as something else? I'll wait.

questions.question: Which address is the file being emailed to?
questions.why: The screen showed a Mail compose screen with the exported audio file attached, requiring a destination address to send the file.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to specify their own email address to receive and download the exported track.
questions.check: Which address does the To field show, and is it the account's own address?
questions.say_example: This is about to email the track to <a typed address>, not your own account. Send it there, or change the address? I'll wait.

questions.question: Where is the email you just tried to send?
questions.why: The banner explicitly states the email couldn't be sent and was saved to the Outgoing folder, which now shows a red badge in the sidebar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: You lose the chance to realize your track failed to share and manually locate the unsent message to try again.
questions.check: Does the banner state the email failed to send and was moved to the Outgoing/Drafts folder?
questions.say_example: Email failed to send - it's sitting in Outgoing

questions.question: Do the notifications about the file attachment agree with each other?
questions.why: A toast notification states the file couldn't be found, but a dialog box immediately after prompts to download the attachment.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses certainty about whether the exported track was actually attached and shared successfully.
questions.check: Does the toast notification's message match what the follow-up dialog says about the attachment?
questions.say_example: One message says the file couldn't be found, the next asks you to download it - they don't agree

questions.question: Which project should you select from the library?
questions.why: The library lists multiple projects, including a newly saved one at the top marked 'Just now'.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the ability to ensure the correct, most recent version of their project is selected for exporting or sharing.
questions.check: Which project, marked as most recent, is shown selected from the library list?
questions.say_example: Selected the project marked 'Just now'

questions.question: Did a confirmation show the file saved to the chosen destination?
questions.why: The screen shows the share sheet opening but does not show the final selection or confirmation of the file being saved.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses certainty that the track was successfully exported and saved to a usable location.
questions.check: Is there a frame confirming the destination was chosen and the file save/send completed, or does the recording stop at the share sheet opening?
questions.say_example: Share sheet opened, but no confirmation of the save ever showed

questions.question: Does the downloaded file name match the project name you set earlier?
questions.why: The screen shows the project being renamed to '[project]' and the resulting download named '[project]_ mix.mp3', confirming the export is correctly labeled.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user loses the assurance that their exported track will be consistently named and easy to identify outside the production tool.
questions.check: Does the downloaded file's name match the project name that was set, allowing for a standard suffix?
questions.say_example: Project is named <Night Drive> but the download is called <Untitled_mix.mp3>

questions.question: Is the project open now the same one that was saved earlier?
questions.why: The project saved at 06:46 does not appear in the project list at 06:51, and the file opened at 07:02 has a different duration than the beat imported at 01:16.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The user receives a disjointed workflow where the final output does not actually reflect the work done during the session.
questions.check: Does the project saved earlier still appear in the project list, and does a file opened later match the duration of what was worked on before?
questions.say_example: The project saved earlier isn't in the list anymore, and the file open now runs a different length

questions.question: Did the exported file actually save to the intended folder, and is it larger than 0 bytes?
questions.why: DAWs can sometimes fail silently during export due to disk space or permission issues, leaving a 0-byte file or no file at all despite showing a completed progress bar.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: The agent might report the task as complete without verifying that a playable audio file was actually generated and saved successfully.
questions.check: Does the file browser show the exported file in the target folder with a non-zero file size?
questions.say_example: The exported file shows <0 bytes> - the export didn't actually write anything

questions.question: Do you have any new alerts or collaboration invitations?
questions.why: Checking the Notifications tab, which currently shows "No notifications yet" under the "Invites" sub-tab, ensures you haven't missed any collaboration requests before starting your work.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this means you miss the opportunity to personally review and manage your collaboration invites from other musicians on the platform.
questions.check: Does the Invites sub-tab show any pending collaboration invites, or does it read 'No notifications yet'?
questions.say_example: No pending invites showing

questions.question: Do you want to update any details on your public profile?
questions.why: The screen shows your current username, talents, and favorite genres, which represent your identity on the platform.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: An agent would likely skip reviewing or updating these details, missing the chance to personalize your public presence.
questions.verify_form: The agent looked at your public profile - check whether it changed anything; that page is what everyone else on the platform sees.
questions.check: Were the username, talents or favorite-genres fields on the public profile changed?
questions.say_example: Updated the public profile - genres now say <lo-fi, ambient>

questions.question: Do you want to invite any collaborators to work on this project?
questions.why: The Collaborators panel on the right edge of the screen allows you to send email invites to other musicians to co-create the track.
questions.whatTheAgentLoses: Delegating this step means losing control over exactly which friends or community members are granted access to co-create your music.
questions.verify_form: The agent opened the invite panel - check whether it sent an invitation and to whom; a collaborator can edit the project.
questions.check: Is an email invite about to be sent to a named collaborator for edit access to this project?
questions.say_example: About to give a collaborator edit access to this project. Send the invite, or hold off?
